```{python}
#| tags: [parameters]
# The parameters and their defaults. Another segment:
#   quarto render segment.qmd -P factor:job -P segment:retired
factor = "age_band"  # "age_band" or "job", a factor in outputs/segments.csv
segment = "60+"      # one segment of that factor, as written in outputs/segments.csv
```

```{python}
#| label: setup
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import HTML

from acme_eval import params
from acme_eval.claims import claim

summary = json.loads(Path("outputs/summary.json").read_text())
metrics = pd.read_csv("outputs/metrics.csv")
segments = pd.read_csv("outputs/segments.csv", dtype={"segment": str})
factor, segment = params.segment(factor, segment, segments)  # stops on an unknown segment

best = summary["best_version"]
overall = metrics[metrics["version"] == best].set_index("metric")["value"]
claim(best == metrics[metrics["metric"] == "roc_auc"].set_index("version")["value"].idxmax(),
      "The best release named here has the highest ROC AUC in metrics.csv.")
rows = segments[(segments["factor"] == factor) & (segments["segment"] == segment)]
here = rows.set_index("version").loc[best]
claim(here["n"] > 0, "The segment has contacts in the test set.")

who = f"aged {segment}" if factor == "age_band" else f'with the job "{segment}"'
name = f"age band {segment}" if factor == "age_band" else f"job {segment}"


def percent(share: float, digits: int = 1) -> str:
    """A share between 0 and 1, as a percentage."""
    return f"{100 * share:.{digits}f}%"


def compare(mine: float, theirs: float, show) -> str:
    """ "above", "below" or "level with", decided on the printed values, and guarded."""
    a, b = show(mine), show(theirs)
    shown = (float(a.rstrip("%")), float(b.rstrip("%")))
    word = params.relation(*shown)
    claim({"above": shown[0] > shown[1], "below": shown[0] < shown[1],
           "level with": shown[0] == shown[1]}[word], f"{a} is {word} {b}.")
    return word


rate_word = compare(here["base_rate"], summary["base_rate"], percent)
called_word = compare(here["share_called"], summary["top_share"], percent)
recall_word = compare(here["recall_top10"], overall["recall_top10"], percent)
```

This page covers the contacts **`{python} who`** (segment: `{python} name`), under
**`{python} best`**, the release that ranks best. Acme Signals is a fictional company; the
bank data are real, and every number here is computed from them by `scripts/evaluate.py`.

## Who they are

Of the `{python} f"{summary['test_rows']:,}"` contacts held out from training,
`{python} f"{here['n']:,}"` are contacts `{python} who`
(`{python} percent(here['n'] / summary['test_rows'])`).
`{python} percent(here['base_rate'])` of them subscribed, `{python} rate_word` the
`{python} percent(summary['base_rate'])` of all contacts.

## How the model treats them

The call centre calls the top `{python} percent(summary['top_share'], 0)` of the ranked list.
That list includes `{python} percent(here['share_called'])` of these contacts,
`{python} called_word` the `{python} percent(summary['top_share'], 0)` of all contacts, and
reaches `{python} percent(here['recall_top10'])` of their subscribers,
`{python} recall_word` the `{python} percent(overall['recall_top10'])` it reaches overall.

```{python}
#| output: asis
if pd.isna(here["roc_auc"]):
    print("The ROC AUC within the segment is not defined: its test contacts all have the "
          "same outcome.")
else:
    auc_word = compare(here["roc_auc"], overall["roc_auc"], lambda v: f"{v:.3f}")
    print(f"Within the segment, the ROC AUC is {here['roc_auc']:.3f}, {auc_word} the "
          f"{overall['roc_auc']:.3f} of the whole test set: it says how well the model orders "
          "these contacts among themselves.")
if here["subscribers"] < params.FEW_SUBSCRIBERS:  # the caveat is chosen by the count
    print(f"\n\n**Few subscribers.** Only {here['subscribers']:,} of these contacts subscribed, "
          "so the recall and the ROC AUC above rest on few people and could move by many points "
          "in another sample. No interval is computed for a segment.")
else:
    print(f"\n\n{here['subscribers']:,} of these contacts subscribed. No interval is computed "
          "for a segment, so a difference of a point or two from the overall figures may be "
          "sampling noise.")
```

::: {#tbl-releases}

```{python}
table = rows.set_index("version")[["share_called", "recall_top10", "roc_auc"]]
table = pd.DataFrame({
    "Release": table.index,
    "Share called": table["share_called"].map(percent),
    f"Recall, top {percent(summary['top_share'], 0)}": table["recall_top10"].map(percent),
    "ROC AUC": table["roc_auc"].map(lambda v: "not defined" if pd.isna(v) else f"{v:.3f}"),
})
HTML(table.to_html(index=False))
```

Each release on the test contacts `{python} who`: the share of them in the called list, the
share of their subscribers it reaches, and the ROC AUC within the segment. Real data: the UCI
Bank Marketing test set.
